rows.label: Concept
rows.text: Dimensions are the grammar of physics: every quantity reduces to powers of M, L, T — force $MLT^{-2}$, work $ML^2T^{-2}$, power $ML^2T^{-3}$, pressure $ML^{-1}T^{-2}$. The **principle of homogeneity** demands the same dimensions in every term of a correct equation, which powers the four uses of dimensional analysis: verifying equations ($s = ut + \frac{1}{2}at^2$ and $v^2 = u^2 + 2as$ both check out), deriving…

rows.label: Formula
rows.text: - Unit conversion: n₂ = n₁ (M₁/M₂)ᵃ (L₁/L₂)ᵇ (T₁/T₂)ᶜ for quantity MᵃLᵇTᶜ - Force = MLT⁻²; Work = ML²T⁻²; Power = ML²T⁻³; Pressure = ML⁻¹T⁻² - G = M⁻¹L³T⁻²; h = ML²T⁻¹; Surface tension = MT⁻²

rows.label: Conditions
rows.text: **Dimensionally correct vs physically correct:** homogeneity is necessary but not sufficient — $s = ut + \frac{1}{3}at^2$ is dimensionally correct yet physically wrong (the ⅓ should be ½).  ·  **Work vs torque:** both have dimensions $ML^2T^{-2}$; dimensional analysis cannot tell them apart.

rows.label: Quick concepts
rows.text: **Homogeneity is a necessary, not sufficient, condition:** it can reject wrong equations but cannot prove right ones.

rows.label: Key points
rows.text: Principle of homogeneity: every term of a correct equation has the same dimensions.  ·  Uses: check equations, derive relations, convert units ($n_2 = n_1(M_1/M_2)^a(L_1/L_2)^b(T_1/T_2)^c$), find units of constants.  ·  Limitations: no dimensionless constants; no added different-dimension terms; no trig/exp/log arguments; identical dimensions not distinguished.

rows.label: Universal facts
rows.text: The seven base dimensions are M, L, T, I (current), Θ (temperature), N (amount), J (luminous intensity) — most mechanics problems need only the first three.
